name: POST /api/inbound/email - mail relay delivers a raw message
description: Called by the mail relay (in AWS: SES receipt rule + forwarder), not by users. Header X-Inbound-Key: the shared relay key; optional X-Envelope-To: the envelope recipients (so Bcc works). Body: the raw message. The project is found from the recipient address; the message is stored and answered 202 at once, then parsed within seconds: sender must be a firm member or allowed sender, DMARC must not have failed, each attachment is type-checked and malware-scanned and becomes a file version (source email). Covers: a per-project forwarding email address accepts attachments into the project within 2 minutes. The happy path needs the relay key (a server secret) and a raw RFC 822 body, which JSON test cases cannot send; expect it to be marked manual after the first run (verified with a scripted relay: allowed sender stored, duplicate Message-ID stored once, stranger and DMARC-fail refused, executable refused, replaced and turned-off addresses answer 404).
